title: Structural analysis of Sphingobium yanoikuyae P4 carboxylesterase reveals conformational and catalytic determinants for PET biodegradation.
authors: Bhatt, Sunidhi; Akhter, Yusuf; Chatterjee, Subhankar
one_liner_zh: 该文通过序列分析、分子对接、500ns分子动力学模拟、MM/PBSA及DFT计算，系统表征了Sphingobium yanoikuyae P4羧酸酯酶降解PET的结构与催化机制，属于蛋白质结构计算研究，方法上结合物理模拟与电子结构计算，对PET降解酶工程有直接参考价值。
abstract: The accumulation of poorly biodegradable polyethylene terephthalate (PET) in the environment has become an emerging ecological and health problem, with a strong need to develop environmentally friendly, biobased degradation methods. This in silico study demonstrates the structural and mechanistic characterization of a carboxylesterase from the phthalate-degrading Sphingobium yanoikuyae P4 for its potential to catalyze the hydrolysis of PET. Sequence analysis of the amino acid residues revealed the conserved alpha/beta-hydrolase fold and the sequence motifs GXSXG and GGX, typical of PET-active enzymes, with evolutionary conservation of the active-site residues. Structural similarity to known PET hydrolases, such as a carboxylesterase from Thermobifida fusca and lipase from Streptomyces exfoliatus, suggested the conservation of the catalytic scaffold. The defined PET backbone oligomer and the hydrolysis intermediates BHET and MHET docked at the same catalytic site with the scissile ester in an ideal conformation for the nucleophilic attack of the Ser215-His418-Glu332 catalytic triad and also stabilized by the Gly217 oxyanion hole. Further, the molecular dynamics simulation for 500 ns supported the stability of the catalytic core of the enzyme-substrate complex, and MM/PBSA revealed a binding free energy of -14.03 kcal/mol, which was strongly affected by van der Waals interactions. Free-energy landscape and principal-component analyses found a flexible, low-energy dominant state in which the loop is mobile, and DFT single-point calculations showed that the catalytic center is electronically well-defined and preorganized. Collectively, these analyses indicate that S. yanoikuyae P4 carboxylesterase possesses the structural and mechanistic prerequisites for PET hydrolysis, providing a candidate scaffold for further experimental and protein-engineering studies.
abstract_zh: 环境中难降解的聚对苯二甲酸乙二醇酯（PET）的积累已成为一个新兴的生态和健康问题，迫切需要开发环境友好、基于生物降解的方法。这项计算机模拟研究展示了一种来自降解邻苯二甲酸盐的Sphingobium yanoikuyae P4的羧酸酯酶的结构和机制特征，以评估其催化PET水解的潜力。氨基酸残基的序列分析揭示了保守的α/β-水解酶折叠以及序列基序GXSXG和GGX，这些是PET活性酶的典型特征，且活性位点残基在进化上保守。与已知PET水解酶（如来自Thermobifida fusca的羧酸酯酶和来自Streptomyces exfoliatus的脂肪酶）的结构相似性表明催化支架的保守性。定义的PET骨架寡聚体及水解中间体BHET和MHET对接在同一催化位点，可裂解酯键处于理想构象，便于Ser215-His418-Glu332催化三联体的亲核攻击，并由Gly217氧阴离子孔稳定。此外，500 ns的分子动力学模拟支持了酶-底物复合物催化核心的稳定性，MM/PBSA分析显示结合自由能为-14.03 kcal/mol，这主要受范德华相互作用影响。自由能景观和主成分分析发现了一个柔性、低能的主导状态，其中环区具有移动性，而DFT单点计算表明催化中心在电子层面定义明确且预组织良好。综合这些分析表明，S. yanoikuyae P4羧酸酯酶具备PET水解的结构和机制前提，为进一步的实验和蛋白质工程研究提供了候选支架。
